Read, validate, and reformat a sample annotation table

Source: R/annotation.R
read_annot.Rd

Reads the annotation csv, strips .d/.raw extensions from Source_file (if present), checks that the required columns are present, harmonizes the data-folder column across search engines (see below), normalizes Sample_peaks to match PEAKS' own export-naming behavior (hyphens/spaces replaced by underscores), and sets factor levels for every character column from the row order in the csv — this is what gives downstream plots/tables their condition/sample ordering.

Usage

read_annot(file_annot)

Arguments

file_annot

Path to a csv file with the annotation table, including at least the columns Condition, BioReplicate, TechReplicate, Sample, and one of Sample_folder (preferred) / Sample_fp / Sample_peaks.

Value

The annotation data frame, with Source_file extensions stripped, Sample_folder/Sample_fp/Sample_peaks all populated (Sample_peaks with hyphens/spaces normalized to underscores), and every character column converted to a factor ordered by first appearance.

Details

One annotation format for every software. The column naming the data subfolder of each sample is Sample_folder, whatever the search engine. The historical, engine-specific names are still accepted: a table providing Sample_fp (FragPipe/DIA-NN/custom) or Sample_peaks (PEAKS) loads unchanged. Whichever is present, the others are derived: Sample_fp is a verbatim copy of Sample_folder, and Sample_peaks is a copy with PEAKS' hyphen/space normalization applied — so the loaders, which key on Sample_fp/Sample_peaks, keep working either way. A column the user supplied is never overwritten.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
read_annot(file.path("1_documentation", params$AnnotationFile))
} # }
